 How to Apply for Financial Aid at the University of Miami 
 From required forms to key deadlines, here's what you need to know before and after submitting your financial aid application. 
 By UM Admission 
 10-29-2026 
 How to apply for need-based financial aid at UM:
 Indicate your interest in need-based financial aid when you submit the  Common Application .
 Complete the  FAFSA  and  CSS Profile , as applicable.
 Submit the required income and financial documentation.
 Meet the financial aid deadline associated with your  admission plan .
 Monitor your  Applicant Portal  and email for additional document requests.
 Once a student’s demonstrated financial need is determined, the Office of Student Financial Assistance and Employment develops a financial aid offer. This offer may include scholarships, grants, loans, work-study, or other assistance, depending on eligibility and available funding.
 Eligible full-time undergraduate students seeking need-based financial aid must submit the FAFSA and CSS Profile, along with required income and wage documentation, by the deadline associated with their admission plan. The deadline to apply for financial aid for students who apply Early Decision I or Early Action is November 15. Students who apply Early Decision II or Regular Decision have until January 5.
 Non-U.S. citizens and non-permanent residents do not ned to complete the FAFSA but must submit the CSS Profile to the College Board by the stated deadline. International students with questions about financial aid should contact intladmission@miami.edu .
 What is the difference between the FAFSA and the CSS Profile?
 The FAFSA determines eligibility for federal and applicable State of Florida need-based financial aid, while the CSS Profile helps determine eligibility for University of Miami institutional grants.
 These applications are needed if a student indicated interest in need-based aid on the Common Application. The FAFSA uses only custodial parent information and is completed to determine domestic student need-based aid eligibility from the federal government and the State of Florida (if applicable).
 The CSS Profile is used to determine eligibility for UM grants for both domestic and international students. The CSS Profile also involves both custodial and non-custodial parent household information. 
 Do students need to complete both the FAFSA and CSS Profile to receive financial aid?
 The FAFSA and CSS Profile are required to be considered for need-based types of financial aid from the State of Florida, the federal government, and UM. 
 International applicants who indicated on their Common Application that they were interested in need-based aid only complete the CSS Profile.
 Note: Neither form is required for consideration for UM merit scholarships. All incoming first-year students are considered for merit scholarships when they submit their application for admission on the Common Application. Students who want to be considered for our Premier Scholarships , which cover up to the full cost of attendance annually, must apply for admission by the November 1 deadline.
 When should students submit the FAFSA and CSS Profile?
 Students must submit their forms by the deadline associated with their admission plan. Early Decision I and Early Action applicants should have the forms and income verification submitted to I-DOC, the College Board's financial records collection portal, by November 15. Early Decision II and Regular Decision applicants have until January 5. 
 New UM applicants who apply on time and receive aid upon admission typically receive an offer reflecting their maximum aid eligibility. 
 What should a student do if their family’s financial situation has changed since the tax year that was used on the FAFSA or CSS Profile?
 Once UM has received the original FAFSA, CSS Profile, and the previous year’s tax records, you should contact the Office of Student Financial Assistance and Employment to provide details on the changes in your family's financial circumstances.
 The Financial Aid team can guide you through the appeal process if your circumstances warrant a change in need-based aid eligibility. Note that reductions in 2026 income may require the filing of 2026 taxes before an appeal can be reviewed.  
 When will students find out how much financial aid they are receiving, and what should they pay attention to when reviewing their financial aid offer?
 If a student meets all of the UM deadlines and accurately submits all requested financial records, and gets admitted to UM, their financial aid offer will likely be available with their admission decision. This would include all known federal and state aid, any UM merit award, and any eligible UM grant aid. 
 This offer may include scholarships, grants, loans, work-study, or other assistance, depending on eligibility and available funding. Unlike scholarships and grants, loans generally require repayment, while work-study funds are earned through employment.
 Students must notify UM of every outside scholarship award via our scholarship submission page , regardless of if it is paid to them or directly to UM. Outside scholarships could have an effect on other financial aid. 
 Note: Students should not subtract a work study award from their expected charges as these funds are not billing deductions. The award funds a student's paycheck if they secure an on-campus work study position. 
 How will you know if there was an issue processing a document or if something is missing? 
 After the University of Miami processes your Common Application, you'll gain access to your Applicant Portal . From there, you will see a link to "View Financial Aid" which opens the Net Partner financial aid portal. There, you can review what is on file, what is missing, and if there are any additional requirements.
 Check the Net Partner financial aid portal often and make sure you review it with your family. 
 Documents you submit through the College Board's I-DOC system will appear in the Net Partner portal after a short processing time. You may also see requests for other documents that aren't in I-DOC. If so, follow the instructions listed in the portal to submit them.
 What should a student do if they’re concerned about affording the University of Miami?
 Understand that the Cost of Attendance is an estimate and not what they will be billed for.
 Speak to a financial aid team member about their options at UM and explain any changes in financial circumstances. 
 Apply for a few dozen outside scholarships very early in their senior year of high school. Most outside scholarships can be used at any university.
 When making your decision, talk to your support system and find a school that is the right financial fit for your undergraduate studies. 
 💡 Read more about how to avoid common financial aid application errors, and stay on top of additional document requests from UM.
